one_liner: Masklet drift rate in SAM2 is predictable from first-frame single-image ambiguity before any tracking happens.
problem: Video object segmentation failures appear frame-by-frame, but the community treats drift as a temporal phenomenon; it may be pre-determined by initial mask ambiguity.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-object drift rate (IoU decay slope over frames) is predicted (r>0.6) by frame-0 measurements alone (prompt-jitter variance, head disagreement), meaning drift is mostly ambiguity amplification, not accumulating temporal error.
why_important: Enables pre-flight triage of which objects need human keyframing before wasting tracking compute, and reorients drift research from temporal machinery to initial disambiguation.
why_possibly_novel: Prediction of temporal failure from purely static initial measurements is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On DAVIS/MOSE, regress observed drift slopes on frame-0 ambiguity features; compare against motion-based predictors.
main_risk: Drift may be dominated by discrete events (occlusions) that no frame-0 signal can foresee.

one_liner: SAM2 re-identification after occlusion falls off a cliff, not a slope: map the memory-horizon discontinuity.
problem: How re-acquisition probability depends on occlusion duration is unmeasured; a cliff vs gradual decay implies different mechanisms (buffer eviction vs feature fade).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: re-ID success is roughly flat until an occlusion-length threshold tied to the memory-bank capacity/eviction rule, then collapses discontinuously - and the threshold moves when memory size is reconfigured, causally implicating eviction policy rather than appearance change.
why_important: A sharp, configurable failure boundary is exactly what deployment safety cases need, and the causal knob test tells us what to redesign.
why_possibly_novel: Occlusion-duration response curves with memory-size interventions are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Procedurally insert variable-length full occlusions into videos, plot re-ID rate vs duration for 3 memory configurations.
main_risk: Entangled confound: longer occlusion often co-occurs with more scene change; synthetic occluders control this.

one_liner: Test whether SAM2 tracks appearance or location: teleport experiments separating the two.
problem: When target and distractor swap positions between frames, does SAM2 follow the pixels or the place? The relative weighting of location prior vs appearance matching is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at low frame rates or after cuts, SAM2 follows spatial location over appearance (segmenting whatever now occupies the old position) with probability rising as inter-frame displacement grows - i.e. its memory attention degrades into a location prior under temporal sparsity.
why_important: Determines trustworthiness on cut-heavy or low-fps footage (surveillance, wildlife cameras, medical cine loops).
why_possibly_novel: Teleport/swap causal probes are standard in psychology, rare for VOS models. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Construct swap/teleport clips from static images (two similar objects exchanging positions with controlled gaps), measure follow-the-object vs follow-the-place rates.
main_risk: Synthetic cuts may be OOD; validate on natural cut footage with manual GT.

one_liner: SAM2 masklets shrink over time: an erosion bias in memory-conditioned decoding.
problem: Anecdotally, tracked masks lose thin parts and extremities over long sequences. Whether there is a systematic signed area bias (erosion vs dilation) and what causes it is unstudied.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the signed relative-area error of SAM2 masklets trends negative over time, concentrated at high-curvature and thin regions, because memory features average over past masks and act as a low-pass shape filter - falsifiable by measuring area drift on constant-size rigid objects.
why_important: Systematic bias (unlike variance) is correctable post-hoc if characterized; also matters for measurement uses (lesion tracking, plant growth).
why_possibly_novel: Signed morphological bias analysis of memory-based VOS is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Track rigid constant-scale objects (fixed camera) for 500+ frames, plot signed area and per-curvature-bin boundary offset vs time.
main_risk: Bias might be dataset-specific (motion blur correlates with extremities), needs controlled rigid-object footage.

one_liner: Distractor-swap probability in SAM2 is a logistic function of feature-space similarity between target and distractor - fit the curve.
problem: Identity switches to similar-looking instances are the canonical multi-object failure, but there is no quantitative model of when they happen.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: swap probability during a crossing event follows a logistic curve in embedding cosine similarity between target and distractor, with a threshold that is stable across videos - giving a predictive, per-scene identity-risk score computable before tracking.
why_important: Predictive risk scoring for identity switches would let pipelines pre-allocate human checks in crowded scenes (cell tracking, sports, herds).
why_possibly_novel: A fitted psychometric-style swap curve for memory-based VOS is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Mine crossing events in MOSE/OVIS, log embedding similarity and swap outcome, fit and cross-validate the logistic.
main_risk: Similarity measured with the model's own embedding may be circular; test external embeddings too.

one_liner: SAM2 accuracy is non-monotonic in frame rate: temporal aliasing hurts fast periodic motion at intermediate fps.
problem: Everyone assumes more fps is better or at worst neutral. For periodic or oscillating motion, intermediate sampling may alias into confusing pseudo-motion.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for objects with periodic motion (wings, wheels, machinery), tracking quality vs frame rate has a dip where sampling aliases the motion (near integer ratios of motion period), recoverable by either higher fps or, counter-intuitively, lower fps.
why_important: Frame-rate is a controllable deployment knob; a non-monotonic law changes how people configure cameras and subsample videos for annotation.
why_possibly_novel: Temporal-aliasing analysis of memory-based segmentation trackers is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: High-fps source videos of periodic motion, subsample at many rates, plot J&F vs rate; look for aliasing dips at predicted ratios.
main_risk: Effect may be confined to a narrow class of scenes; scope must be honest.

one_liner: Memory poisoning: quantify how one corrupted frame propagates through SAM2's memory bank - is error injection sub- or super-linear?
problem: Robustness of memory-augmented trackers to single-frame corruption (glare, compression burst, occluder) is unmeasured; the memory could either dilute or amplify a bad write.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a single adversarially bad mask written to memory degrades subsequent frames super-linearly in time for ambiguous targets (self-reinforcing retrieval) but is diluted for distinctive targets - the bifurcation is predicted by target-distractor similarity.
why_important: Determines whether memory needs write-gating/quarantine, and defines a concrete attack surface for safety-critical tracking.
why_possibly_novel: Error-injection response analysis of segmentation memory banks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Inject controlled mask corruptions at frame t, measure IoU trajectories after t vs matched controls across target types.
main_risk: Injection method may not represent natural corruption; use both synthetic and natural (glare/blur) events.

one_liner: Which frame you prompt matters more than how well you prompt it: middle-frame prompting beats first-frame in long videos.
problem: The universal convention prompts frame 0. Information-theoretically the best anchor frame is the one minimizing appearance distance to the rest of the video.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: prompting the medoid frame (closest to all others in feature space) improves whole-video J&F more than upgrading the frame-0 prompt from 1 click to a perfect mask - anchor selection dominates prompt quality beyond a video-length threshold.
why_important: Zero-cost accuracy gains for every SAM2 pipeline, and reframes interactive video annotation as a frame-selection problem first.
why_possibly_novel: Anchor-frame optimality vs prompt-quality tradeoff quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On LVOS/long videos, compare first-frame perfect-mask vs medoid-frame single-click prompting under matched budgets.
main_risk: Medoid selection needs the whole video (offline only); streaming variant may lose the effect.

one_liner: VOS metrics reward temporal smoothness, not correctness: an oracle temporal smoother improves J&F without new information.
problem: If post-hoc smoothing of masks (no access to images) improves benchmark scores, the metric partially measures smoothness style rather than segmentation quality.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a model-free temporal mask smoother (shape-consistent filtering of existing predictions) improves J&F on standard VOS benchmarks by a nontrivial margin for many methods, and method rankings change when evaluation adds unsmoothable per-frame probes - demonstrating metric gaming headroom.
why_important: If rankings are partially smoothness rankings, years of architecture conclusions need re-reading; also a cheap test-time trick that should be disclosed.
why_possibly_novel: Smoothing-only ablation as a metric audit for VOS is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Apply temporal morphological smoothing to frozen predictions of 5 public methods, report J&F deltas and rank flips.
main_risk: If gains are negligible the audit vindicates the metric (still worth publishing as a check).

one_liner: Recency-based memory is provably wrong for periodic scenes: diversity-sampled memory should beat recency at equal size.
problem: SAM2-style memories favor recent frames. For periodic or revisiting content (orbiting views, back-and-forth motion), recency discards the most predictive exemplars.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched memory budget, exemplar selection by appearance-diversity (k-center over frame features) outperforms recency on videos with periodicity/revisits, while recency wins on smooth-drift videos - a measurable regime split that current fixed policies straddle badly.
why_important: Identifies a principled scene-conditional memory policy question rather than a bigger-memory arms race.
why_possibly_novel: Regime-mapped comparison of memory selection policies in promptable video segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Reconfigure SAM2 memory selection at inference (no retraining) with diversity sampling; evaluate on periodic vs drift video subsets.
main_risk: Inference-time policy swap without retraining may be off-manifold for the memory attention.

one_liner: Does temporal context help or hurt on static camouflaged objects? SAM2 vs per-frame SAM on motionless targets.
problem: Temporal models are assumed to help always. For a static camouflaged animal, memory frames add no new information but may add noise accumulation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on static targets in moving-texture scenes (wind, water), SAM2's memory hurts relative to independent per-frame segmentation of the anchor mask, because background texture change is misread as object change - temporal context has a sign-flipping value depending on motion source.
why_important: Establishes when video machinery should be bypassed - important for camouflage, surveillance, and medical cine where targets barely move.
why_possibly_novel: Signed value-of-temporal-context analysis conditioned on motion source is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: MoCA-Mask static-segment subset: compare SAM2 propagation vs frozen anchor mask + per-frame refinement under matched prompts.
main_risk: Truly static targets are rare in benchmarks; may need curated clips.

one_liner: Topology-change events (splitting, merging, pouring) are an unhandled event class in video segmentation - build the taxonomy and measure failure.
problem: Masklets assume persistent object identity, but real objects split (dough, cells, liquids) and merge. What trackers do at these events is uncharacterized.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at split events, memory-based trackers deterministically follow the larger fragment (area-weighted attention), losing the smaller one at a rate predicted by fragment area ratio - a simple law that a fragment-aware evaluation would expose.
why_important: Cell biology, cooking/robotics, and material handling all need split/merge tracking; knowing the default failure law is step one.
why_possibly_novel: An event-taxonomy benchmark for topology changes in VOS is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Curate 100 split events (cell videos, cutting food), measure which fragment retains identity vs area ratio.
main_risk: Annotation ambiguity about which fragment 'is' the original; needs a convention.

one_liner: Joint multi-object tracking in SAM2 degrades per-object accuracy vs independent runs: measure memory contention.
problem: SAM2 tracks multiple objects with shared compute/memory. Whether objects interfere (contention) or help (context) compared to isolated single-object runs is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-object J&F drops as tracked-object count rises even without spatial interaction, and the drop concentrates on objects sharing appearance clusters - evidence of representational contention in shared memory attention rather than mere occlusion effects.
why_important: Determines scaling behavior for dense-instance video annotation and whether parallel independent runs (costly) are secretly necessary.
why_possibly_novel: Contention-vs-context decomposition with non-interacting object sets is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On multi-object videos, compare joint tracking vs one-object-at-a-time runs on identical prompts; stratify by pairwise similarity.
main_risk: Implementation details (per-object memory in SAM2) may already isolate objects; verify against the actual architecture first (KNOWN: SAM2 keeps per-object state; contention could still arise via shared backbone resolution and NMS-like interactions).

one_liner: Camera-zoom sequences reveal scale lag: memory features anchor to old object scale and delay mask growth.
problem: During zoom (optical or dolly), object scale changes smoothly, but memory frames encode stale scales. Scale-adaptation dynamics of memory trackers are unquantified.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: under monotonic zoom, SAM2 mask area lags true object area with a measurable time constant proportional to memory length, producing systematic under-segmentation during zoom-in and over-segmentation during zoom-out.
why_important: Zoom is ubiquitous (broadcast, drones, microscopy autofocus); a signed predictable lag is correctable but only if characterized.
why_possibly_novel: Scale-lag time-constant measurement for memory trackers is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Synthesize exact-zoom sequences from high-res stills (crop pyramids), measure mask-area lag vs zoom rate and memory length.
main_risk: Synthetic zoom lacks parallax; confirm on real dolly footage subset.

one_liner: Forward-backward tracking asymmetry as a free uncertainty signal: where the two directions disagree, the tracker is wrong.
problem: Tracking a video forward vs backward should ideally give the same masks; divergence indicates unreliability, but this self-consistency signal is not exploited or characterized for modern VOS.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: forward-backward mask disagreement per frame predicts actual error (AUROC>0.85) better than model confidence outputs, and the asymmetry is directional - errors accumulate on the direction that first encounters ambiguity - enabling label-free error localization in time.
why_important: Gives annotation pipelines an automatic 'inspect here' signal, cutting human video-QA cost.
why_possibly_novel: Cycle-consistency is classic for optical flow (KNOWN); its calibration as an error detector for memory-based masklets is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run SAM2 both directions on DAVIS/MOSE from the same anchor, correlate disagreement with per-frame IoU error.
main_risk: Backward tracking may fail identically on the same hard segments, blinding the signal exactly where needed.

one_liner: Occlusion boundary ownership errors: SAM2 assigns the occluder's edge to the occluded object during partial occlusion.
problem: When object A passes in front of B, B's visible-region boundary is A's silhouette. Whether video segmenters represent this distinction (boundary ownership) is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: during partial occlusions, the tracker's boundary error on the shared edge is asymmetric - the occluded object's mask systematically 'sticks' to the occluder's silhouette even after separation begins (measurable hysteresis in boundary release), revealing absence of ownership representation.
why_important: Boundary ownership is the core of amodal reasoning; a measurable hysteresis gives a concrete probe for whether models have any occlusion model at all.
why_possibly_novel: Boundary-release hysteresis as an amodal-representation probe is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Curate crossing events with GT, measure shared-edge error before/during/after separation, quantify release lag in frames.
main_risk: Requires accurate GT at occlusion boundaries, the noisiest annotation region.

one_liner: Micro-motion as a segmentation cue: can temporal aggregation segment objects invisible in any single frame (breathing, vibration)?
problem: Some objects are single-frame-invisible but reveal themselves through sub-pixel periodic motion. Current video segmenters aggregate over time yet nobody tests whether they exploit micro-motion.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM2 and peers extract near-zero information from sub-pixel periodic motion (performance equals static-frame baseline), while an explicit temporal-amplification preprocessing (Eulerian-style) makes the same targets segmentable - locating a concrete representational gap between possible and actual temporal use.
why_important: Defines an entire class of targets (hidden animals, machinery defects, breathing patients under blankets) where temporal information is the ONLY signal.
why_possibly_novel: Micro-motion segmentation as a benchmark task is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search; motion magnification itself is KNOWN (Wu et al., Eulerian Video Magnification).
minimal_experiment: Collect/synthesize clips with sub-pixel oscillating targets, compare SAM2 vs SAM2-on-motion-amplified input.
main_risk: Amplification also amplifies noise; careful SNR-controlled synthesis needed.

one_liner: Once lost, always lost: quantify whether SAM2 failure is an absorbing state and what spontaneous recovery requires.
problem: Practitioners report that after a tracker loses its target, it rarely recovers without re-prompting, but recovery statistics have never been formalized.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM2's per-frame recovery probability after a loss event is <5% and roughly constant (memoryless), so expected lost-time is geometric and long - and recovery events are almost exclusively triggered by the object re-entering high-similarity poses to memory exemplars, not by search behavior (the model has no search).
why_important: Absorbing-state failure changes deployment math: the metric that matters is time-to-loss, not average IoU; also motivates re-detection modules with clear expected value.
why_possibly_novel: Survival-analysis treatment of masklet life/death/recovery is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run long videos (LVOS), detect loss events (IoU<0.1), fit survival and recovery hazard curves.
main_risk: Loss definition threshold shapes conclusions; report sensitivity across thresholds.

one_liner: Fit the memory-size vs drift power law: how much memory buys how much tracking longevity?
problem: Memory capacity is a compute knob without a published scaling relationship; teams size it by folklore.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: median time-to-loss scales as a power law in memory slots with exponent <1 (diminishing returns), and the exponent differs by scene type (crowded vs sparse), so optimal memory allocation is scene-conditional and mostly small.
why_important: Turns an arbitrary hyperparameter into a budgeted engineering decision with published curves.
why_possibly_novel: Scaling-law methodology applied to tracking memory rather than model/data size is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sweep memory configurations on LVOS/MOSE, fit time-to-loss curves per scene category.
main_risk: Architecture may not expose memory size cleanly without retraining; may need the open-source variants.

one_liner: Equal-budget video annotation: sparse clicks on many frames beats a perfect mask on one frame.
problem: The standard video annotation protocol (dense mask on frame 0, then propagate) has never been tested against spreading the same human-time across the video as sparse corrections.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched human-seconds, K single-click corrections spread over the video outperform one dense frame-0 mask by a growing margin with video length, because temporal information (where drift happens) is worth more than spatial precision (pixel-perfect anchor).
why_important: Could halve real-world video annotation cost with zero model changes - protocol science rather than architecture.
why_possibly_novel: Budget-matched protocol comparisons for video annotation are rare; UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Simulate both protocols with timed human cost models on DAVIS/LVOS + SAM2, then a small real-annotator study (5 people).
main_risk: Human time models for clicks vs masks vary; the real-annotator confirmation is essential.

one_liner: Ultrasound video breaks SAM2's memory attention because speckle decorrelates: modality-specific drift signature.
problem: SAM2 memory matches features across frames. Ultrasound speckle decorrelates within milliseconds while anatomy persists - the opposite statistics of natural video.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM2 drift on ultrasound cine is dominated by speckle decorrelation (drift correlates with speckle decorrelation rate, not anatomical motion), so mild despeckling preprocessing improves tracking MORE than fine-tuning the model on ultrasound masks at matched effort.
why_important: Ultrasound is the highest-volume medical video modality; identifying the true bottleneck (input statistics vs model weights) redirects adaptation effort.
why_possibly_novel: Attribution of medical-video tracking failure to speckle statistics vs anatomy is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On CAMUS/echo videos, correlate frame-pair feature similarity with speckle decorrelation; compare despeckled input vs LoRA-tuned model at matched cost.
main_risk: Despeckling may destroy diagnostic boundaries; need boundary-quality co-evaluation.

one_liner: Self-diagnosing drift onset: within-track feature statistics detect the exact frame where a masklet starts failing.
problem: Drift detection currently needs ground truth or human review. The track's own feature stream (memory attention entropy, mask-embedding velocity) may mark failure onset.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a change-point detector on the masklet's internal statistics localizes drift onset within +-5 frames for a majority of failures, without images or GT - failure has an internal signature preceding visible error.
why_important: Automatic QA for large-scale video auto-annotation (SA-V style) - review only flagged spans instead of whole videos.
why_possibly_novel: Change-point analysis on tracker internals as self-diagnosis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Log internal statistics over DAVIS/MOSE runs, train change-point detector, evaluate onset localization against GT-derived failure times.
main_risk: Gradual drifts may lack a change point; report by failure type.

one_liner: Shot-change as a natural memory-reset probe: what SAM2 retains across cuts tells us what its memory encodes.
problem: Across a hard cut, low-level correspondence dies but object identity may persist (same object, new view). SAM2 behavior at cuts is an untested window into memory content.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM2 survival across cuts is predicted almost entirely by pose/scale similarity of the object across the cut and not by scene continuity, showing memory encodes object-centric appearance templates rather than scene context.
why_important: Edited video (film, broadcast, social media) is most of watched video; cut robustness defines applicability, and the probe clarifies representation content.
why_possibly_novel: Using editing structure as a controlled representational probe is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble cut pairs with graded object-pose and scene changes (from multi-view datasets), measure survival rates per condition.
main_risk: SAM2 may fail at essentially all cuts, flattening the analysis (still a clean negative result).

one_liner: Sub-frame mask interpolation: do memory features support generating masks BETWEEN frames (temporal super-resolution)?
problem: Applications need masks at higher temporal rates than compute allows (or between saved keyframes). Whether tracker features interpolate linearly in time is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: interpolating SAM2 memory/mask embeddings between frames yields valid intermediate masks whose error grows sub-linearly with gap size for smooth motion - i.e. the learned representation is approximately temporally linear, enabling 4-10x cheaper video segmentation via keyframing + latent interpolation.
why_important: Direct compute savings for video pipelines and a fundamental finding about temporal geometry of the learned space.
why_possibly_novel: Latent temporal interpolation for masklets is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On high-fps videos, decode masks from interpolated embeddings at held-out timestamps, compare vs true frames and vs mask-space (pixel) interpolation baselines.
main_risk: Embedding space may be far from linear; pixel-space interpolation might trivially win.

one_liner: Background persistence pollution: in fixed-camera streams, background objects entering memory create recurring false positives.
problem: Surveillance-style fixed cameras repeatedly show the same background structures; if any frame's mask leaks onto background, memory can immortalize the leak.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: in fixed-camera long streams, false-positive persistence (same wrong region recurring across frames) accounts for the majority of accumulated error - unlike moving-camera video where errors are transient - implying stationarity is a distinct and unmodeled failure regime for memory trackers.
why_important: Fixed cameras dominate real deployments (traffic, retail, wildlife, factory QA) yet benchmarks are handheld/moving; a regime-specific error structure would show benchmarks mis-sample reality.
why_possibly_novel: Error-recurrence analysis conditioned on camera stationarity is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run SAM2 on fixed-camera datasets (VIRAT-like), measure spatial autocorrelation of errors over time vs handheld controls.
main_risk: Fixed-camera GT for masks is scarce; may need semi-automatic GT with heavy review.
